To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
uncarboxylate osteocalcin, a protein produced by the bone, stimulates 25-hydoxy vitamin D production by the Leydig cell line, through a GPR6C6a-dependent mechanism.

uncarboxylate osteocalcin (ucOC), a hormone produced by osteoblasts, increases the production of 25-hydroxivitamin D (25-OHD) in Leydig cells, the main testosterone-producing cells in the testis, by a GPRC 6a-dependent pathway.

uncarboxylate osteocalcin, the active form of the bone protein osteocalcin, stimulates the vitamin D 1α-hydroxylating enzyme CYP2R in Leydig cells through the receptor GPRC 6A, a G protein-coupled receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new players in the cross talk between the testis and the bone.
the identification and characterization of the mechanisms by which OC regulates the production of 25-OHD in the testis.
the cross talk between bone and testis and its possible impact on male health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bone-testis cross talk involves a direct action of ucOC on CYP2 R1 expression in Leydig cells through a GPR6C6A-dependent pathway.
the Leydig cells are capable of producing 25-OH-Vit D, and this production is regulated by LH and ucOC through GPRC6.
the bone testis cross talk involves a complex network of hormones, including OC, which is produced by osteoblasts, and CYP2R, which is produced in Leydig cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
OC, a bone-derived factor, is able to regulate CYP2R-1 expression through GPRC6-A and to stimulate 25-OH-Vit D synthesis in Leydig cells.

the cross talk between the testis and bone is not limited to the production of testosterone and insulin-like 3, but it also involves the production of 25-OHD.

Leydig cells are involved in the regulation of Vit D metabolism and that the bone-testis axis is a possible target for Vit D therapy.
